findings.title: Leftover debug logging at Error level, including the full list of IDs, runs on every cleanup batch.
findings.body: Every batch logs two `r.log.Error` lines, and one of them includes the full `ids` slice. The same lines are at 554/557 and 576/579. The last batch of each loop returns zero rows, so a healthy cleanup with nothing to delete still writes at least two error lines per annotation type and for tags. With the 1-minute ticker this happens every minute, and with a large batch size (for example 32767) each line carries tens of thousands of IDs. That floods error logs, sets off error alerting, and the `err` field in the first line is always nil. Remove these lines, or lower them to Debug and drop the `ids` field.

findings.title: Building the ID list with repeated Sprintf takes quadratic time.
findings.body: On SQLite with a batch size above 999, each ID is added by `fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)`, which copies the whole string built so far. A 32767-ID batch copies several gigabytes in total, and this runs for every batch on every cleanup cycle. Build the string with `strings.Builder`, or join `strconv.FormatInt` results with `strings.Join`.

findings.title: The cleanup interval for every cleanup job drops from 10 minutes to 1 minute.
findings.body: This ticker drives `srv.clean`, which runs all the cleanup jobs, not only annotation cleanup. Each job now runs 10× as often, which adds steady database load on every instance. The deadlock fix the PR asks for does not need this, and the PR description does not justify it. It looks like a leftover from local testing. Restore the 10-minute interval, or make the annotation interval configurable on its own.

findings.title: The subtest cleanup is registered only after the inserts and count checks succeed.
findings.body: All subtests share one DB, and `createTestAnnotations` now inserts fixed IDs starting at 1. If an insert or one of the count assertions fails in a subtest, `t.Cleanup` is never registered and the rows stay in the database. Every later subtest then fails on duplicate primary keys or wrong counts, which hides the original failure. Fix: register the `t.Cleanup` before calling `createTestAnnotations`.
